issues.title: A Neo4j HTTP `tx/commit` request keeps the writes of its successful statements when another statement fails, and runs the statements after the failure
issues.assessment: An HTTP batch with a failed statement commits successful writes and continues after failure; the read-only gate correctly prevents all writes.
issues.expected: [access.http_transactions](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.http_transactions): one `tx/commit` request is one transaction that keeps its writes only if every statement succeeds; a server that cannot do this must refuse a request it could commit only in part. Sources: the route's own name (`/db/neo4j/tx/commit`, Neo4j's HTTP route that opens and commits a transaction in one request); ADMIN_API's Neo4j HTTP routes and its read-only rule, which already treats the request as one unit ("runs none of its statements"); the same rule the product's Bolt surface owns ([access.bolt.transactions](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.transactions)), which `theorem_http_rule_is_bolt_rule` derives the batch rule from (BEGIN, the statements, COMMIT). Neo4j's HTTP API documentation is not quoted: fetching it was denied in this session, as in the review's (limitation); the rule above rests on the product's own documents and its Bolt rule. Which repair (one transaction, or refusing multi-statement requests) is the open question [access.transactions](open_questions.md#access.transactions).
issues.severity_basis: a client that sends a multi-statement request as one unit of work and gets 400 back cannot tell that the statements before and after the failure were committed; a retry of the request writes them again. Medium rather than High (unlike [bug-plt-127](#bug-plt-127)): the persisted partial write is the same class, but the client is told that the request failed (status 400 and an `errors` entry), so it is not silent; the departure needs a request that mixes a failing statement with writes.
